story.title: Kachru's Strange Song
paragraphs_en: K achru Singh Patel and his wife Radha lived in the village of Prahladpur. Kachru Singh would spend the entire day gazing at the sky and sleeping. Meanwhile, Radha would get up before dawn, rush to catch the train to the city and then go from one house to another, cooking. The kind Madams and Sirs often offered her food to take back home. Radha would return to the village in the afternoon and share the leftovers with her husband.

One day, Radha brought back some dosa batter. Kachru, snoring under the shade of a jamun tree near their hut saw Radha and started grumbling about starving the entire day. Hungry herself, Radha began preparing the dosas. While greasing the hot pan, she thought, “This greedy man will wolf down the dosas without thinking about my share. Maybe I should make my dosas later. But what if he sees them then? Let me make all six now and give him three.”

She poured some batter on the pan. When the batter started bubbling, she turned it over to cook on the other side. Radha repeated this process six times. Every time a dosa was ready, she removed it and splashed water on the hot pan, making it sizzle. She poured some batter on the pan. When the batter started bubbling, she turned it over to cook on the other side. Radha repeated this process six times. Every time a dosa was ready, she removed it and splashed water on the hot pan, making it sizzle.

She gave three hot and fluffy dosas to Kachru who gobbled it up in no time. After a ferocious burp, he asked Radha for more. Radha replied, “Oh, but there are no more left.” “Oh, but I know you made six dosas!” Kachru Singh said.

Radha stood there amazed and confused. How could her lazy husband know this? Kachru Singh said, as if he knew exactly what she was thinking, “Oho, you think I am just a lazy no-gooder, don’t you? When I lie down under the jamun tree, I meditate and pray to the gods. I am now in possession of magical powers. I hear more than others, I see more than others, I know more than others." Radha did not believe a word her husband said. She took her share of dosas to her friend Rohiya’s house and over the yummy meal, they laughed together at Kachru Singh’s nonsense.

Soon, the word spread in Prahladpur and everyone was talking about Kachru Singh Patel’s magical powers. A few days later, Kachru was resting under the tree as usual. Rohiya’s baby son was playing near his house with a noisy rattle.

Suddenly, baby Aniruddha began howling. Rohiya came and picked him up. “What has upset you? Where is your toy?” She looked here and there but could not find the rattle anywhere. By evening, there was hullabaloo in the village. Rohiya had declared the rattle to be missing and nobody could find it. In tears, she went to Kachru Singh Patel. “If it is true that you have magical powers, help me find my rattle. It is made of real silver and was given by Aniruddha’s great-great-great grandmother.”

Kachru Singh made a big show of consulting the gods. He began singing a strange song. I was listening when the dosas sizzled, sizz-sizz-sizzle. Each dosa said, sizz-sizz-sizzle. Then he announced, “Go look in the thickest shrub between your house and mine.” Lo! The silver rattle was found and everyone considered it fortunate that such a powerful man lived in their village.

One night, there was chaos. Guddu, the old dhobhi of the colony, could not find his beloved donkey Kaidai. He went to Kachru Singh Patel’s house. “Please help me! Kaidai is gone!" One night, there was chaos. Guddu, the old dhobhi of the colony, could not find his beloved donkey Kaidai. He went to Kachru Singh Patel’s house. “Please help me! Kaidai is gone!"

Kachru Singh agreed and asked for a day’s time because the donkey god Daikai Dev was available only in the mornings. The next day, Kachru Singh woke up before his wife and headed out. He began looking for Kaidai everywhere. A few men with camels were going through the village. One of the men was saying, “Let’s not stop here. There is a small lake nearby. There will be grass for the camels there and a tree’s shade for us.” Kachru Singh began following them. When he reached the lake, lo! Guddu’s donkey was fast asleep on lush grass.

Kachru Singh woke the donkey up and tried to make him move. But Kaidai refused to budge. Kachru Singh sat down, exhausted. Nibbling on a blade of sweet grass, he began singing. Kachru Singh woke the donkey up and tried to make him move. But Kaidai refused to budge. Kachru Singh sat down, exhausted. Nibbling on a blade of sweet grass, he began singing.
I was listening when the dosas were sizz-sizz-sizzling I was looking at the noisy rattle when it was fall-fall-falling and I looked for Kaidai where lush grass was grow-grow-growing.

Kaidai got up suddenly with a loud bray. Kachru Singh led him back to the village and handed him over to an ecstatic Guddu who couldn't believe his eyes and ears. By now, the word had spread far and wide. One early morning, the mayor of a nearby city came searching for Kachru Singh Patel … but, that’s another story. Perhaps you would like to hear it from Kachru Singh himself. He sits under the same jamun tree in Prahaladpur, singing a strange song about sizzling dosas.

items.text_en: K achru Singh Patel and his wife Radha lived in the village of Prahladpur.
Kachru Singh would spend the entire day gazing at the sky and sleeping.
Meanwhile, Radha would get up before dawn, rush to catch the train to the city and then go from one house to another, cooking.
The kind Madams and Sirs often offered her food to take back home.
Radha would return to the village in the afternoon and share the leftovers with her husband.
One day, Radha brought back some dosa batter.
Kachru, snoring under the shade of a jamun tree near their hut saw Radha and started grumbling about starving the entire day.
Hungry herself, Radha began preparing the dosas.
While greasing the hot pan, she thought, “This greedy man will wolf down the dosas without thinking about my share.
Maybe I should make my dosas later.
But what if he sees them then?
Let me make all six now and give him three.”
She poured some batter on the pan.
When the batter started bubbling, she turned it over to cook on the other side.
Radha repeated this process six times.
Every time a dosa was ready, she removed it and splashed water on the hot pan, making it sizzle.
She poured some batter on the pan.
When the batter started bubbling, she turned it over to cook on the other side.
Radha repeated this process six times.
Every time a dosa was ready, she removed it and splashed water on the hot pan, making it sizzle.
She gave three hot and fluffy dosas to Kachru who gobbled it up in no time.
After a ferocious burp, he asked Radha for more.
Radha replied, “Oh, but there are no more left.” “Oh, but I know you made six dosas!” Kachru Singh said.
Radha stood there amazed and confused.
How could her lazy husband know this?
Kachru Singh said, as if he knew exactly what she was thinking, “Oho, you think I am just a lazy no-gooder, don’t you?
When I lie down under the jamun tree, I meditate and pray to the gods.
I am now in possession of magical powers.
I hear more than others, I see more than others, I know more than others." Radha did not believe a word her husband said.
She took her share of dosas to her friend Rohiya’s house and over the yummy meal, they laughed together at Kachru Singh’s nonsense.
Soon, the word spread in Prahladpur and everyone was talking about Kachru Singh Patel’s magical powers.
A few days later, Kachru was resting under the tree as usual.
Rohiya’s baby son was playing near his house with a noisy rattle.
Suddenly, baby Aniruddha began howling.
Rohiya came and picked him up.
“What has upset you?
Where is your toy?” She looked here and there but could not find the rattle anywhere.
By evening, there was hullabaloo in the village.
Rohiya had declared the rattle to be missing and nobody could find it.
In tears, she went to Kachru Singh Patel.
“If it is true that you have magical powers, help me find my rattle.
It is made of real silver and was given by Aniruddha’s great-great-great grandmother.”
Kachru Singh made a big show of consulting the gods.
He began singing a strange song.
I was listening when the dosas sizzled, sizz-sizz-sizzle.
Each dosa said, sizz-sizz-sizzle.
Then he announced, “Go look in the thickest shrub between your house and mine.” Lo!
The silver rattle was found and everyone considered it fortunate that such a powerful man lived in their village.
One night, there was chaos.
Guddu, the old dhobhi of the colony, could not find his beloved donkey Kaidai.
He went to Kachru Singh Patel’s house.
“Please help me!
Kaidai is gone!" One night, there was chaos.
Guddu, the old dhobhi of the colony, could not find his beloved donkey Kaidai.
He went to Kachru Singh Patel’s house.
“Please help me!
Kaidai is gone!"
Kachru Singh agreed and asked for a day’s time because the donkey god Daikai Dev was available only in the mornings.
The next day, Kachru Singh woke up before his wife and headed out.
He began looking for Kaidai everywhere.
A few men with camels were going through the village.
One of the men was saying, “Let’s not stop here.
There is a small lake nearby.
There will be grass for the camels there and a tree’s shade for us.” Kachru Singh began following them.
When he reached the lake, lo!
Guddu’s donkey was fast asleep on lush grass.
Kachru Singh woke the donkey up and tried to make him move.
But Kaidai refused to budge.
Kachru Singh sat down, exhausted.
Nibbling on a blade of sweet grass, he began singing.
Kachru Singh woke the donkey up and tried to make him move.
But Kaidai refused to budge.
Kachru Singh sat down, exhausted.
Nibbling on a blade of sweet grass, he began singing.
I was listening when the dosas were sizz-sizz-sizzling I was looking at the noisy rattle when it was fall-fall-falling and I looked for Kaidai where lush grass was grow-grow-growing.
Kaidai got up suddenly with a loud bray.
Kachru Singh led him back to the village and handed him over to an ecstatic Guddu who couldn't believe his eyes and ears.
By now, the word had spread far and wide.
One early morning, the mayor of a nearby city came searching for Kachru Singh Patel … but, that’s another story.
Perhaps you would like to hear it from Kachru Singh himself.
He sits under the same jamun tree in Prahaladpur, singing a strange song about sizzling dosas.
